rationale: This is a strictly monotone (outer RANK) re-encoding of the archived `peer_relative_harvest_with_slack`, so it re-proposes an already-evaluated signal with identical firm ordering and, as the author concedes, identical portfolio statistics — a diagnostic on FMB regressor distribution, not a new economic signal.

Averaging the slack and asset-vintage moderators is a genuinely different construction from either archived triple product, though the archive is internally contradictory about the sign of ppent/ppegt (`profitable_old_capital_base` treats low net-to-gross as the good state, `harvest_with_young_capital_runway` the opposite) and the vintage leg carried essentially no cross-sectional slope (fmb 0.14), so noise reduction is speculative.

A weakest-link gate is not a monotone transform of the product and so constitutes a substantively different aggregation of the same three legs, giving a clean test of whether the alpha lives in the extreme corner or in joint moderate satisfaction — though it remains a functional-form experiment on well-trodden legs rather than new economics.

Pairing the archive's best-slope profitability leg with its best-alpha moderator is the obvious and defensible next step and is not a rediscovery, but it is an incremental recombination of two evaluated signals, and the claimed benefit of the inert outer RANK applies only to the FMB regression, not to the alpha.

Decomposing net-debt-to-assets into a cash-coverage moderator is a real attribution test that can distinguish a distributable-cash mechanism from a low-leverage style tilt, and the depreciation floor sensibly handles debt-free firms, though cash-holdings premia are themselves a documented anomaly that could partly account for any gain.

The expression multiplies a leg whose standalone expected sign is positive (peer-relative profitability improvement) by an investment leg expected negative and then asserts an unambiguously negative composite sign, so the predicted direction is not implied by the construction; moreover profitable-high-investment underperformance is essentially the published q-theory investment anomaly conditioned on profitability.
